we propose a fully distributed continuous-time algorithm for generalized Nash games in a partial decision setting, which is based on consensus dynamics and primal dual gradient methods, and can be adapted to the specific class of aggregative games.
we provide a fully distributed continuous time algorithm for generalized Nash equilibrium seeking in multi integrator games, and that we extend our results to generalized aggregative games.

we propose fully distributed continuous time algorithms for generalized aggregative Nash equilibria seeking in multi integrator agents, that can be tuned without the need of any global information, and that are based either on fixed or on dynamic gains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of fully distributed continuous time algorithms, with or without adaptation, that drive a group of agents playing games on an undirected graph to generalized Nash equilibria.

, in this paper, we have designed a set of continuous time controllers, both with constant or adaptive weights, that can be used in a fully distributed fashion by each agent to drive the agents in a generalized aggregative game, to a generalized Nash Equilibrium, in a continuous time setting, under mild assumptions on the game mapping.

, for the first time in the literature, the problem of distributed generalized Nash equilibrium (GNE) seeking in continuous-time is tackled for multi integrators, in both the constant and adaptive gain cases, and in aggregative games, both with constant or adaptive gains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, we provide distributed algorithms for generalized aggregative and non aggregative games, with constant and adaptive weights, and we prove their convergence under mild conditions on the game mapping.
we design continuous time distributed controllers, based on primal dual gradient dynamics and consensus protocols, to solve fully distributed generalized Nash games in a networked setup.

we design fully distributed continuous-time controllers, based on primal dual gradient dynamics and consensus algorithms, to drive the (multi) integrators agents to a Generalized Nash Equilibrium (GNE), in the context of generalized aggregative games, and we show convergence to GNE, under Lipschitiz continuity and strong monotomicity of the game.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, by leveraging the structure of the multi integrator agents, we are able to design fully decentralized controllers that drive the agents to an equilibrium, without any global information.
generalized Nash equilibria can be sought by agents with limited information, without the need to solve the game explicitly.
, for the first time, fully distributed algorithms for continuous time generalized Nash equilibrium seeking are presented.
